interpretations: "Films in stock" means the count of distinct films (film_id) that have at least one inventory copy, grouped by rating. The result is the sum of those counts over ratings above the across-rating average. It also gives the average excess over that average
"Films in stock" means the count of inventory copies (inventory rows), grouped by rating. The result is the sum of those copy counts over ratings above the average. It also gives the average excess

"Films in stock" means distinct films, but only for films with inventory in a given store, counted per store and then combined across stores. The above-average comparison is made on the combined total
The "average rating" means the mean of the per-rating counts, which is the total divided by 5. This is the unweighted average across the 5 rating groups
The "average rating" means the mean count per rating, computed only over ratings that have at least one film in stock
The "average rating" means the average over all films in the film table, including films with no inventory. Ratings are compared to this figure
The "total films in stock across those above-average ratings" means the sum of the per-rating counts for ratings above the average
The "total films in stock across those above-average ratings" means the count of distinct films across those ratings. This is the same as the sum, because each film has one rating
"On average, how far above" means the mean of (rating count − average count) across the above-average ratings, as an absolute difference in number of films
"On average, how far above" means the mean percentage or ratio excess over the average, as a relative difference
"On average, how far above" means the total excess divided by the number of all ratings, not only the above-average ones
"Above" means strictly greater than the average. Ratings equal to the average are excluded
"Above" means greater than or equal to the average, so ratings equal to the average are included
"No rounding" means the average excess is returned as the full-precision decimal value, with no ROUND applied
"No rounding" means the average excess is returned as an exact fraction or integer-division result without any truncation or casting
"Films in stock" means films with currently available inventory. This excludes copies that are currently rented out, where the rental return_date is NULL
"Films in stock" means inventory copies that have never been rented, or copies whose latest rental has been returned
The existing interpretations cover most readings. These are missing:
The "average rating" means the average count of the other ratings, leaving out the rating being compared (a leave-one-out average)
The "average rating" means the average copies per film (inventory copies divided by distinct films in stock), compared against each rating's count
The "average rating" means the average over per-store, per-rating counts (store and rating combinations), rather than over the 5 ratings

"Films in stock" means distinct films with at least one copy that is currently available (not rented out), counted per rating. This combines the distinct-film and availability readings, which the existing list only treats separately

"On average, how far above" means the difference between the mean count of the above-average ratings and the overall average. This is the same value as the mean excess, but computed as a difference of means
"On average, how far above" means the total film count of the above-average ratings minus the average, i.e., the sum's distance from the average rather than the mean per-rating excess
queries:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS n
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
a AS (
  SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM c
)
SELECT SUM(c.n) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(c.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess
FROM c, a
WHERE c.n > a.avg_n;
WITH c AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM inventory i
  JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
a AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM c
)
SELECT SUM(c.cnt) AS total_films_in_stock,
       AVG(c.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS average_excess
FROM c, a
WHERE c.cnt > a.avg_cnt;
WITH per_store AS (
  SELECT fc.category_id, i.store_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.film_id) AS films
  FROM inventory i
  JOIN film_category fc ON fc.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY fc.category_id, i.store_id
),
totals AS (
  SELECT category_id, SUM(films) AS films_in_stock
  FROM per_store
  GROUP BY category_id
)
SELECT c.name
FROM totals t
JOIN category c ON c.category_id = t.category_id
WHERE t.films_in_stock > (SELECT AVG(films_in_stock) FROM totals);
SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM film GROUP BY rating);
SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS cnt FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating)
